reference.title: Lateral Step-up
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower slowly.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short hold, about 2 s down

prescription.tempo: Up in about 1 s, down in about 2 s

cues.text: Stand side-on to the box with the right foot flat on top, hands on hips.
Breathe out and push down through the right heel to straighten the leg; the left foot lifts beside the box.
Stand tall on the right leg, pelvis level, left foot hovering.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the left heel just taps the floor.
Tap, do not rest; go straight into the next rep. Switch legs after the set.

mistakes.fix: Keep the floor foot light; lift it as soon as the box leg starts to push.

mistakes.mistake: Hip dropping on the free side
mistakes.fix: Keep the pelvis level; squeeze the side of the box-leg hip.
Keep the knee over the 2nd-3rd toe.

kinematics.norm: 15-40 cm in studies: 15 cm (MacAskill 2014), 20 cm (Worrell 1998), 40 cm (Muyor 2020)
Bent at the start, fully straight at the top (Muyor 2020; MacAskill 2014)
Level, shifting sideways over the box foot (clinical opinion)
Metronome-paced, about 2 s up and 2 s down in Muyor 2020

sources.title: Worrell, Crisp & LaRosa 1998, electromyographic reliability and analysis of selected lower extremity muscles during lateral step-up conditions (J Athl Train 33(2):156-162; PMC1320404)
MacAskill, Durant & Wallace 2014, gluteal muscle activity during weightbearing and non-weightbearing exercise (Int J Sports Phys Ther 9(7):907-914; PMC4275195)

Muyor, Martín-Fuentes, Rodríguez-Ridao & Antequera-Vique 2020, EMG activity of gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, biceps femoris and the vasti during the monopodal squat, forward lunge and lateral step-up (PLoS ONE 15(4):e0230841)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a stable box that cannot slide or tip.
modify: Knee pain: use a lower box (10-20 cm).
Balance concerns: hold a wall or rail with one hand.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Box-leg knee extensors do most of the work: vastus medialis and lateralis were more active than the hamstrings and gluteus maximus (Worrell 1998) and were the most active muscles in Muyor 2020.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Box-leg knee extensors do most of the work: vastus medialis and lateralis were more active than the hamstrings and gluteus maximus (Worrell 1998) and were the most active muscles in Muyor 2020.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Box-leg hip extensor; activity was about 31% MVIC in an unloaded lateral step-up on a 6-inch step (MacAskill 2014).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Box-leg hip extensor; activity was about 31% MVIC in an unloaded lateral step-up on a 6-inch step (MacAskill 2014).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Holds the pelvis level as the body moves sideways over the box foot; about 61% MVIC in an unloaded lateral step-up (MacAskill 2014).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Holds the pelvis level as the body moves sideways over the box foot; about 61% MVIC in an unloaded lateral step-up (MacAskill 2014).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Steady the thigh and assist the hip as it straightens.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Steady the thigh and assist the hip as it straightens.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the box-leg shin; the floor foot gives only a light push.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the box-leg shin; the floor foot gives only a light push.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall over the box foot.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist side-bending toward the free leg.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist side-bending toward the free leg.

guides.label: Hips rise and shift over the box foot
Box knee straight at the top
